verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The paper writes the Faà di Bruno term structure of a mixed space-time derivative of χ(aq) with q = q(z,t): a prefactor a^k χ^{(k)}(aq) times a product of k derivatives of q whose multi-indices sum to (a',b'). No Lean declaration forms that expansion. What the repository states instead is (i) the exact one-variable chain rule `scaledCutoff_iteratedDeriv`, iteratedDeriv n (scaledCutoff a) q = a^n · χ^{(n)}(a q) — this is the paper's term in the degenerate case where q is itself the variable, so every ∂q factor is 1 and only k = n survives; (ii) the k = 1 case for a genuine composite χ(q(w.1,·)), as the `have hc` step at GenericSolenoidalRealization.lean:81, giving ∇(χ∘q) = χ'(q)·∇q; and (iii) for general order, the norm-level composition bound `composition_jet_bound` (a wrapper of Mathlib's norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_le), ‖D^m(g∘f)‖ ≤ m!·C·D^m, which is what `cutoff_jet_bound` actually uses to reach the same conclusion without ever naming the individual chain-rule terms. There is also no z/t split: the Lean works with one total Fréchet order throughout. The surrounding result (the derivative bound of the next display) is proved, so the missing expansion costs nothing.
